source_title: Arsenal v Benfica: Women’s Champions League – live
source_excerpt:
Alessia Russo made history after scoring a hat-trick in Arsenal’s win over Benfica at Meadow Park
4d ago GOAL! Arsenal 3-0 Benfica (Russo 79)
4d ago GOAL! Arsenal 2-0 Benfica (Russo 66)
4d ago GOAL! Arsenal 1-0 Benfica (Russo 39)
4d ago GOAL! Arsenal 3-0 Benfica (Russo 79)
4d ago GOAL! Arsenal 2-0 Benfica (Russo 66)
4d ago GOAL! Arsenal 1-0 Benfica (Russo 39)
The brilliant Alessia Russo scored a hat-trick to give Arsenal a comfortable win over Benfica at Meadow Park. In the process she overtook Fran Kirby as the leading English goalscorer in the WCL. Arsenal have tougher fixtures ahead but right now, for all their domestic travails, they are second in the Champions League.
Turns out there was an offside in the build up. As you were.
Icing, meet cake. Caitlin Foord scores Arsenal’s fourth with a cool finish after Russo’s cross is half blocked at the near post.
86 min The match is petering out. Arsenal have some tough games to come – Barcelona, Lyon, Inter – but this puts them in a good position to qualify for the knockout rounds.
82 min I think this will be the first time Arsenal have won consecutive games in 2026-27.
A hat-trick for Alessia Russo! She curls the penalty high into the net, with Pauels going the wrong way.
76 min Stanway marches through midfield and plays an excellent through pass to Foord, who is tripped by Amado. A clear penalty.
76 min Pauels makes another good save, pushing away a fierce snapshot from Olivia Smith.
75 min Arsenal lost a 2-0 lead against Paris FC in their last Champions League game. This lead feels a lot more secure.
71 min: Arsenal substitutions Kim Little, Leah Williamson and Emily Fox replace Taylor Hinds, Kyra Cooney-Cross and Elisa De Almeida.
70 min “I guess every game, for every team – when things aren’t going well, and frustration is growing – will have a moment or two when the fans sit back, breathe out, and offer up a prayer of thanks,” says Charles Antaki. “In too many games for it to be healthy, Arsenal relies on just one person. So once again: thank heavens for Alessia Russo.”
69 min And now Arsenal almost make it 3-0. Reuteler walks round the keeper Pauels and has a shot cleared off the line.
68 min Benfica almost get one back with a nice strike from the substitute Norton that is pushed round by Rodriguez.
Alessia Russo has made history! She becomes the leading English goalscorer in the WCL after scoring her second goal of the night. Catley curled an inswinger into the six-yard box, where Russo headed emphatically past Pauels. What a lovely moment for a marvellous footballer.
66 min Pauels makes another save, this time to claw Smith’s deflected shot round the near post.
65 min Hinds pings a long-range shot that is comfortably saved.
64 min: Benfica substitution Sabastine and the teenage star Carolina Tristao replace Alves and Csiki
63 min Russo shoots straight at Pauels from 10 yards, a great chance to make it 2-0.
63 min As well as being the name of a cracking Neil Finn album, one-nil is an awkward lead. Arsenal are on top but won’t feel truly comfortable unless they get a second.
59 min Smith’s cross is headed over at the near post by Russo. She thought it hit the head of Gomes but the referee gave a goalkick.
58 min Pauels makes a fine close-range stop from Foord, though it wouldn’t have counted as she was offside.
56 min Batlle’s deep cross from the right is headed back into the six-yard box by Foord. It’s just behind Russo and Benfica force the ball clear.
54 min Lyon are 2-0 up at home to Inter in tonight’s other game. Marie-Antoinette Katoto scored both goals in the first half.
51 min Arsenal have made a strong start to the second half and look of a mind to wrap this up sooner rather than later.
48 min Amado makes a goal-saving challenge on Foord, who looked set to score after controlling a beautiful pass from Cooney-Cross.
46 min Back underway at Meadow Park. Benfica have brought on Andreia Norton for Pauleta.
Alessia Russo’s excellent finish has given Arsenal a deserved lead at Meadow Park. Benfica had one great chance, missed by Froya Dorsin, but for the most part Arsenal were the better team.
45 min Pauels makes another decent save, diving low to her left to push Russo’s long-range shot round the post.
41 min That was Russo’s 21st goal in the WCL, which equals Fran Kirby’s record for an England player.
Arsenal worked the ball down the left , with Catley and Hinds involved at the start. Foord flicked a clever pass round the corner to Russo, who cracked a low shot into the far corner from 15 yards. A ruthless finish from a quite brilliant player.
33 min Batlle skips down the right and crosses towards Smith, who watches the bounce and hits a good shot that is pushed round the near post by the diving Pauels. Excellent stop.
32 min At the other end, Russo drives wide from 16 yards after good play by Smith.
A lamentable backpass from Cooney-Cross puts Dorsin through on goal. She tries to chip Rodriguez but clears the crossbar. What a chance!
Corner to Arsenal on the right. It’s lofted deep towards Russo, whose header is well held by Pauels as she falls to her right. There were Arsenal players waiting for a rebound.
26 min Stanway hits a really good shot from just outside the area that is pushed round by the diving Pauels. Good save.
25 min Moller chops neatly past an Arsenal player and finds Csiki, whose long-range shot dribbles through to Rodriguez.
25 min It’s all a bit cagey. Arsenal have played reasonably well without really threatening to score.
21 min Benfica win their first corner of the game. Bratberg Lund’s inswinger is headed away well by De Almeida.
19 min Nice play from Arsenal. Stanway scoops a pass over the top towards Batlle, who turns a defender and slides a precise low cross back towards Smith. Her first-time shot is blocked.
16 min Smith’s driven free-kick from the right reaches Russo, whose shot on the turn is blocked.
13 min Arsenal have been the better team without threatening to overwhelm Benfica. Long way to go, etc.
10 min A terrific cross from Reuteler on the right is thrashed behind for an Arsenal corner. Not sure who the defender was but they could easily have done an OG.
7 min Another long-range shot from Smith, who has started in a central position, is easily saved by Pauels.
5 min A pretty quiet start to the game, on the field anyway. The small crowd at Meadow Park are making plenty of noise.
2 min Olivia Smith drives a low shot from 20 yards that is comfortably saved by Lena Pauels.
I forgot to say that Benfica are without their excellent Brazilian striker Nycole Raysla because of injury.
1 min Benfica, in white, kick off from right to left as we watch.
The players are ready for action on a crisp, chilly night at Meadow Park. Let’s play!
“Time was, the despondent Arsenal fan could turn away from a poor showing by the men’s team to see something inspiring by the women; serial winners, of course, under the inimitable Vic Akers,” writes Charles Antaki. “But that was then. Now, faced with trying to get over with a night of embarrassment and chagrin – a hopeless, shaming farrago by the men – watching the women’s team isn’t quite the surefire refreshment it once was. In fact, they’ve been deeply disappointing in all their games this season so far. Inspiration needed all round. Call up Vic. Get him to pull his shorts on and step out onto the technical area. Make it yesterday once more.”
You’re two of my favourite MBMers, but I think I’m in Camp Kári on this. Great managers have wobbles, something I wish I knew when I wrote the most moronic piece of my life 20 years ago.
“I was stunned when I read that Renée Slegers was under pressure,” writes Kári Tulinius . “ It’s only just over a year since the greatest triumph in the club’s history, not only winning the Champions League, but beating that Barcelona side. Yes, Arsenal have started horribly, but I think Slegers has shown she’s a great coach.”
“Don’t forget Servette!” writes Jez Smith. “We are at Servette, where we saw our team put in a commanding performance to beat Leuven 5-1. We are, at least briefly, be above the likes of Manchester City. Which feels incredible after our first two defeats in the campaign.”
Ellie Carpenter has put Chelsea 1-0 up at home to Roma , and Momoko Tanikawa has scored Bayern Munich’s second equaliser at home to Real Madrid. Yep.
Renee Slegers makes three changes from the win at Spurs. Elisa De Almeida , Ona Batlle and Geraldine Reuteler come in for Leah Williamson, Emily Fox and Lisa Baum
Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Rodriguez; Batlle, De Almeida, Catley, Hinds; Cooney-Cross, Stanway; Smith, Reuteler, Foord; Russo.
Subs: Borbe, Damm, Fox, Wubben-Moy, Williamson, Little, Baum, Blackstenius, Holmberg.
Benfica (4-3-3) Pauels; Amado, Gomes, Testen, Bratberg Lund; Pauleta, Moller, Csiki; Davidson, Dorsin, Alves.
Subs: Thais Lima, Bihina, Demehin, Norton, Borges, Oliveira, Sabastine, Tristao, Ziqin, Costa, Loucao, Guedes.
The half-time scores in tonight’s early games
Hello, hello and welcome to live coverage of Arsenal v Benfica in the Women’s Champions League. Arsenal will hope their 2-1 win at Tottenham kickstarts a hitherto disappointing season. They’re sixth in the WSL, with two wins from seven, and have four points out of six in the Champions League. It should really be six from six – they led 2-0 away to Paris FC last month before being pegged back .
This is what the head coach Renee Slegers had to say in her programme notes for tonight’s game.
double quotation mark Let’s make Saturday’s success against Tottenham Hotspur the beginning of something. We have been on such a frustrating run of games and to be able to break that cycle on Saturday, at the north London derby no less, meant so much to all of us.
You all deserved that win. Your dedication to this team throughout a difficult start to the season has been nothing short of incredible and we are all so grateful for your support. We wanted to make sure you knew that.
The supporters were on our minds all week in the lead-up to the match. We’d spoken within the group about how everyone wanted to play for something bigger than themselves, and there’s no greater symbol for that than a sold-out away end of nearly 4,000 people. So we said: let’s do this for you. In times like these, actions speak louder than words.
You could see that when Leah sprinted to you the moment the final whistle blew, with Isabella Damm and Amy Liddiard right there in the crowd alongside you. Saturday was an outpouring of relief, but it was also more than that. It was a sign of the connection we share. You are all a part of this team.
